problems.title: A perfect square with a negative input
problems.question: Find $p^2+4pq+4q^2$ for p=23,q=-1.5.
problems.idea: Recognize a squared binomial.

problems.title: Count coins of two values
problems.question: There are 28 coins, worth 89 tetri in total, consisting of 2-tetri and 5-tetri coins. How many are 2-tetri coins?
problems.idea: Let the count of the cheaper coins be x.
steps: The other 11 coins give 34+55=89 tetri, checking the total.

problems.title: Count solutions of nested absolute values
problems.question: How many solutions does $\big||x-6|-6\big|=4$ have?
problems.idea: Split the outer absolute value into its two possible signs.
steps: The first gives x=16,-4; the second gives x=8,4.

problems.title: Match prime powers
problems.question: Find n if $12^n9^3/6^{12}=1$.
problems.idea: Write each base in primes 2 and 3.
steps: A positive base other than 1 has value 1 only at exponent zero, so n=6.

problems.title: Percentage of silver in an alloy
problems.question: An alloy contains 1.6 g of gold and 0.8 g more silver than gold. What percent is silver?
problems.idea: Find the silver mass and divide by the total.

problems.title: Mix two concentrations
problems.question: Mix 3 L of 30% alcohol solution with 5 L of 20% solution. Find the concentration.
problems.idea: Add the pure alcohol amounts, then divide by the total volume.
steps: The pure alcohol amount is 0.3·3+0.2·5=1.9 L.

problems.title: Common divisors of two numbers
problems.question: A and B are the positive divisors of 48 and 64. Find the sum of the elements of A∩B.
problems.idea: Their common divisors are the divisors of their greatest common divisor.

problems.title: A 60-degree bisector in a right triangle
problems.question: The bisector of the 60° angle of a right triangle is 1 cm shorter than the longer leg. Find its length.
problems.idea: Use the 30°-60°-90° side ratio and the angle-bisector length formula.
steps: Write the short leg as t, the long leg as √3t and the hypotenuse as 2t.
The sides next to the 60° angle are t and 2t, so ℓ=2·t·2t·cos30°/(3t)=2√3t/3.
Its excess over ℓ is ℓ/2=1 cm, giving ℓ=2 cm.

problems.title: Perimeter from two circle radii
problems.question: A right triangle has inradius r=1 and circumradius R=5. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: The circumradius gives the hypotenuse.

problems.title: A faster car passes a head start
problems.question: A 60 km/h car starts 2 hours before a 75 km/h car in the same direction. How long after the second starts are they 180 km apart?
problems.idea: Use the absolute difference of their positions.
steps: The two algebraic possibilities give t=-4 and t=20.
Only t≥0 is allowed; the initial lead is only 120 km, so the 180 km separation occurs after the faster car has passed.

problems.title: Slope from the intercept-length ratio
problems.question: The rising line in the diagram cuts off an x-axis segment twice as long as its y-axis segment. Which listed function can represent it?
problems.idea: Use the intercept ratio to find the slope’s magnitude.
steps: The picture has u<0 and v>0, so the slope is positive.
The length condition is |u|=2|v|, giving slope=1/2.
The listed positive-slope function with this value is y=x/2+1.

problems.title: A difference changes at a constant rate
problems.question: Two vessels initially contain 112 and 200 cm³ of water. The first receives 11 cm³/min more than the second. When will it contain 44 cm³ more?
problems.idea: Track the difference, so the individual filling rates cancel.
formulas: Difference at time t=initial difference+(difference of rates)t.

problems.title: Bisect a base angle of an isosceles triangle
problems.question: AB=BC and B=40°. AD bisects angle A, with D on BC. Find ADC.
problems.idea: First find the two base angles.
formulas: Equal sides have equal opposite angles; a bisector halves an angle.
problems.note: The emphasized choices in the source do not change the geometric angle sum.

problems.title: Central angles from two isosceles triangles
problems.question: A,B,C lie on a circle centred at O, arranged as shown. BAO=20°, BCO=30°. Find the marked smaller angle AOC.
problems.idea: The radii make AOB and BOC isosceles.
formulas: In an isosceles triangle, the two base angles are equal; angles around a point sum to 360°.

problems.title: Use the diagram to resolve a mislabeled hypotenuse
problems.question: In the shown right triangle ABC, C=90° and B=38°. D is the midpoint of the hypotenuse AB. A circle passes through A,C,D. Find its minor arc AC.
problems.idea: The hypotenuse midpoint is equally far from all triangle vertices.
formulas: DA=DC for the midpoint of a right triangle’s hypotenuse; an inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.
steps: Triangle ADC is isosceles with DA=DC, so ACD=CAD=52°.
The arc AC opposite D measures 2·76°=152°; it is the minor arc.
problems.note: The text calls AC the hypotenuse and says the circle meets it at its midpoint, which would put three collinear points on a circle. The diagram clearly places D on hypotenuse AB; the solution follows that intended configuration.

problems.title: Solve two shopping equations
problems.question: Two lemons and three oranges cost 1.9 lari; six lemons and four oranges cost 4.2 lari. Find the cost of one of each.
problems.idea: Use elimination to obtain the unit prices.
formulas: If lemon price=L and orange price=O, then 2L+3O=1.9 and 6L+4O=4.2.

problems.title: Count positive integer pairs
problems.question: How many positive integer pairs (x,y) satisfy 3x+5y=100?
problems.idea: Use divisibility by 3 and the positivity bounds.
steps: The allowed values congruent to 2 modulo 3 are 2,5,8,11,14,17.

problems.title: Compare coefficients for an identity
problems.question: If 2ax-3b=5x-1 has infinitely many solutions, find a+b.
problems.idea: The coefficients and constants must match for every x.
formulas: An identity mx+n=px+q requires m=p and n=q.

problems.title: Cancellation in a parameter equation
problems.question: Solve cx-b(c-x)=a(b-x)-b(a-x), where a+c≠0.
problems.idea: Expand both sides and cancel matching terms.
steps: Since a+c≠0, divide to get x=bc/(a+c).

problems.title: Find a product from a linear system
problems.question: Find xy if $(x+y)/2-2y/3=5/2$ and $3x/2+2y=0$.
problems.idea: Clear denominators and eliminate x.
formulas: Multiplying by 6 and 2 respectively preserves the equations.
steps: Subtract the first from the second: 5y=-15, so y=-3.
Then 3x+3=15, giving x=4. The product is -12.

problems.title: An exterior-angle relation forces a right angle
problems.question: One exterior angle of a triangle is 180° less than the sum of the other two exterior angles. Classify the triangle.
problems.idea: Use the sum of all three exterior angles.
formulas: One exterior angle per vertex sums to 360°.
steps: Let the specified exterior angle be e. The other two sum to 360°-e.
The adjacent interior angle is also 90°.

problems.title: A team finishes the remaining work
problems.question: Two teams together could complete a harvest in 12 days. After 8 days together, the first leaves; the second finishes the rest in 7 days. How long would the second need alone?
problems.idea: Find the fraction remaining after the shared work.
steps: Together the teams complete 8/12=2/3 of the job.
The second team completes the remaining 1/3 in 7 days.
Its rate is (1/3)/7=1/21 job per day, so a full job takes 21 days.

problems.title: Three arcs on a semicircle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base angles 56°. A semicircle on an equal side as diameter is divided by the other sides into three arcs. Find the smallest arc.
problems.idea: Use inscribed angles to find overlapping arcs, then subtract from 180°.
formulas: A semicircle measures 180°; an inscribed angle intercepts twice its own measure.
steps: The base angle 56° intercepts 112° of the semicircle, leaving an end arc of 68°.
The apex angle 68° intercepts 136°, leaving the other end arc of 44°.

problems.title: The missing rectangle can have two perimeters
problems.question: A rectangle is split into four rectangles by one horizontal and one vertical segment. Three small perimeters are 4,14,22 m. Find the fourth.
problems.idea: Opposite small perimeters have equal sums, but their positions are not supplied.
formulas: If the widths are a,c and heights b,d, opposite perimeter sums both equal 2(a+b+c+d).
steps: If the 4 m rectangle is opposite the unknown one, the unknown perimeter is 14+22-4=32 m.
If the 14 m rectangle is opposite the unknown one, it is 4+22-14=12 m.
The third pairing gives 4+14-22=-4 m, impossible for a perimeter.
Both positive possibilities can occur with positive rectangle dimensions.
problems.note: No diagram or position condition is supplied. Both of these values are listed and both satisfy the stated data.

problems.title: Repeated dilution of alcohol
problems.question: A barrel initially contains 32 L alcohol. Remove 8 L and refill with water three times in total. How much alcohol remains?
problems.idea: Every replacement retains three quarters of the alcohol present.
